description: The coral brand of Multi-brand: its theme picks in each mode. The loader joins it with scheme.json.

coral.label: Coral
coral.description: Upbeat and energetic: coral orange, Poppins, pill controls.

theme.$description: The Coral theme: what each brand-dependent semantic key picks, in light and dark, plus mode-free picks (fonts, corners) in base. Info uses blue, kept apart from the brand color so it never reads as an action. Categories 1 to 5 are teal, purple, orange, blue, green: distinct hues for tags and chart series, with no meaning. Disabled uses the neutral slate.

open-ds.why: radius.pill: We use a pill corner for Coral's buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a playful tone, by brand convention. A full radius does this by rounding both ends of every Coral button and input into a capsule. So Coral feels upbeat, the roundest of the three brands, because each brand sets its corners (shape.values) on a neutral base (brand.q1).

radius.pill: We use the pill control corner for Coral's badges in order to keep one role family by the badge relation: here badges share the control's corner. The same full radius does this by giving a status the capsule of the buttons. So the shape matches the buttons and the word in each badge marks it as a status, because each brand sets its corners (shape.roles, shape.values).

radius.16: We use a 16px corner for Coral's menu options in order to keep nesting by the relation: the 20px surface corner minus the panel's 4px padding. The inner radius does this by the nesting rule of Aster's option corner, run 4px inside Coral's 20px surface. So an option's curve runs parallel to its menu's curve, because Coral's surfaces take 20px (shape.roles, brand.q1) and the panel's padding is 4px (spacing.values).

radius.12: We use the 12px box corner for Coral's growing boxes in order to keep them box-shaped objects by the relation: a pill control gives way to the box corner. A moderate radius does this by curving the corners while the sides stay straight as the box grows. So a text area stays a box, not an oval, because Coral's controls are pills (shape.values).

radius.20: We use a 20px corner for Coral's cards and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a playful tone by brand convention. A large radius does this by breaking the outline with a wide curve while the sides stay straight. So a plan card reads as one round, friendly object, the roundest of the three brands, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) on a neutral base (brand.q1).
poppins for display text: Each brand brings its own face, Inter, Plus Jakarta Sans or Poppins, on one shared type scale, so brands differ and the system stays one.
